JUDGMENT
The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.03.2022.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 08.03.2023 the petitioner was returning to his home in his Yamaha RX135 motorcycle No. KA-06-Q-2873, when he reached near 5 th Main, Daignal Road Junction, Jayanagara 4th Block, Bengaluru, the Hond CRV Car bearing No.KA-52-P-1954 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained multiple injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Promed Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022 and further admitted on 27.06.2022 to 28.06.2022, undergone operations and discharged with advice to take bed rest.
So far he has spent huge amount towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, running business under the name and style of "Sri Durga Mart and Events" having office at Nagasandra Circle,
Basavanagudi, Bangalore.
He has paid the Income Tax for the income of Rs.5,06,470/- for the assessment year of 2021-22.
Due to the injury and disability he is unable to stand or walk properly.
As such he is not capable of discharging his duties and thus suffered loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notices, respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

The Respondent No.1 owner denied all the averments of the petition except admitting that his vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent as on the date of accident and the policy was valid from 01.05.2022 to 31.03.2023 as on the date of accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle had a valid and effective DL to drive the aforesaid Car.

Further denied the manner of accident, age, avocation,
income, medical expenses etc., Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner prays to dismiss the petition against him.

2
The Respondent No.2 insurance company denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the 1 st respondent in respect of the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.
Further stated that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.
The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
The driver of the offending vehicle had a valid and effective DL to drive the aforesaid Car.
Further stated that the petitioner was not wearing safety head gear to ride the motorcycle as on the date of accident.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the manner of accident, age,
avocation, income, medical expenses etc.,
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, the respondent No.2 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident took place on 08.03.2022 aat about 10.00am near 5th Main, Daignal Road Junction, jayanagara 4th Block,
Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Honda CRV Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.
Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked Ex.P.15 to 20.
In spite of sufficient opportunities, the respondents did not chose to adduce evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of compliant, charge sheet, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, notice u/Sec.133 of MV Act and reply to the same, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 6.

3 9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- Complaint which was lodged on the same day of accident by the petitioner himself.
The said statement was given by the petitioner in the hospital while taking treatment.
The contents of Ex.P.1 is in consonance with the petition averments.
In continuation of investigation, the IO has conducted Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch.
On perusal of the contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch therein, the accident spot is in the left side portion of the junction in which the petitioner was proceeding.

10. On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint, Ex.P3 mahazar and Ex.P4 rough sketch the driver of Car bearing No.KA- 51-P-1954 was coming from 33 cross road and was entering in to 5th main road caused the accident in the left side of 5th main road.

The vehicles which come from cross road and tries to enter the cross road they must be more vigilant and they should give the first preference to the vehicles moving in the main road to pass and thereafter they should enter in to the main road.
The rough sketch depicts the negligence of driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954 who was entering in to the main road.
Thereby the negligence of driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954 stands established in the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.

11. The Ex.P5 is IMV report of the both the vehicles wherein the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954 has got damaged in its front left side bumper, left side cover and right hand indicator and the bike in which the petitioner was proceeding has got damaged in its left side bumper which also once again supported the case of the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.
Thus the Ex.P5 once again successfully established the negligence on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.

Ex.P2 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the offending Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954, wherein, the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.

12. It is very important to note that the respondent No.1 being the owner of CRV Car bearing Reg.No. KA-51-P-1954 even though denied the allegations by filing the written statement does not chosen to lead evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
No grounds are made out by the respondents to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.
13. The respondent No.2- insurance company has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of offending vehicle.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the CRV Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954.
14.

The charge sheet is came to be filed against the respondent No.1 who is the driver and owner of the the offending CRV Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;
2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.

4 Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the CRV Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

sentences.text: 16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent No.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by stating that the accident was occurred by his negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.

18. The contents of Ex.P3 spot mahazar, Ex.P4 rough sketch and Ex.P5- IMV report falsifies the contention of respondent No.2 about the contributory negligence by the petitioner for the occurrence of accident.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P2 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 &
338 of IPC against the driver of the CRV Car bearing Reg.No. KA-51-P-1954.
19.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 08.03.2022 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954. which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.

In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 54 years.
As per the Aadhaar card produced at Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 20.05.1969.
The accident took place on 08.03.2022 hence, as on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 52 years.

As per the discharge summary produced at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioner was admitted to Promed Hospital on 08.03.2022 and discharged on 11.03.2022 again admitted on 27.06.2022 and discharged on 28.06.2022 and he has sustained fracture tibia and fibula left leg.
He underwent closed reduction and interlocking nailing left tibia done under SPA and proximal screw removal done.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.60,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
b) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10, amounting to Rs.1,43,711/-.
At the time of cross-examination suggestions were put to the PW.1 about the reimbursement of medical bills by the health insurance.
The said suggestion is denied by the petitioner stating that the health insurance was done two days before the accident.
So it cannot be claimed.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced health insurance copy.
There is no contrary evidence is available to hold that these bills are reimbursed.
But it is very important to note that Sl. No.1, 2 and 17 bills of Ex.P10 are the advance receipts.
The inpatient bill for the period of 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022 is not produced.
The Sl. No.1and 2 are the advance receipts regarding the payment made towards the final bill for the admission period of 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022.
The final bill of the said period of 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022 is not produced as such the receipts which are made towards the final bill cannot be considered in the absence of final bill.
The Sl No.17 is another receipt paid towards the final bill for the admission period of 27-06-2022 to 28-06-2022.
But the Sl No.18 bill of Ex.P10 is the final bill for the period of 27-06-2022 to 28-06-2022.
Hence the Sl.No.18 bill being the final bill can be reimbursed and Sl No.17 being the receipt of Sl No.18 bill cannot be reimbursed.
The other medical bills are the consultation bills and pharmacy bills which need to be covered under this head.
Accordingly by excluding the bills produced at Sl No.1, 2 and 17 (amounting to Rs.1,10,000/-), the remaining bills amounting to Rs.33,711/- is need to be reimbursed under this head.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement by rounding off to Rs.34,000/- under this head.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was running business under the name and style of Sri Durga Mart and Events.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced licence, receipts etc., to show his exact income.

As per the discharge summary produced at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioner was admitted to Promed Hospital on 08.03.2022 and discharged on Ravichandra vs Satyanarayanaraju K.V on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167755220/
6 11.03.2022 again admitted on 27.06.2022 and discharged on 28.06.2022 and he has sustained fracture tibia and fibula left leg.
He underwent closed reduction and interlocking nailing left tibia done under SPA and proximal screw removal done.

By the injuries and fractures sustained by the petitioner certainly he has to take bed rest and his movements or involvement in his business will be reduced and it effects on his business and in turn on his income.
The petitioner admitted to the hospital on two times ie., from 08.03.2022 and discharged on 11.03.2022 again admitted on 27.06.2022 and discharged on 28.06.2022.
Thereby total 6 days he was hospitalized and thereafter considerable time like three months is needed for the recovery of the injuries.
Thereby the four months of laid up period has to be considered along with 6 days of inpatient period.
No evidence is available to hold the exact income of the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2022.
Therefore, his income will be considered at Rs.15,500/- pm.
As per the discharge summaries at Ex.P.8, he took treatment for 6 days.
Considering his fractures and age, the petitioner is entitled Rs.15,500/- x 4 = Rs.62,000/- under this head.
d) Disability:- The petitioner has stated that he was running the business in the name and style of Durga Mart and Events.
No evidence is placed to show the profession of the petitioner.

In this regard when the PW.1 petitioner was cross-examined he has stated that, still Sri Durga Mart and Events is continuing and in the year 2022-2023 his income was Rs.4,51,870/- and in the year 2023-2024 it was Rs.5,58,040/-.

The answer given by the petitioner in the cross examination is hereby quoted for better appreciation of the point:
"I am the owner of Durga Mart and events.
It is true to suggest that I am Income tax assessee and I am regularly paying tax.
It is true to suggest that by gross income for 2022-23 was Rs.4,51,870/- and for the year 2023-24 was Rs.5,58,040/-.
It is true to suggest that the Sri Durga Mart and events is still running.
Witness further states that during corona they were running Grocery also but not that portion of the shop is closed''.
The said answers given by the PW.1 reveals that even after the accident his income is not reduced and he being the owner of Durga mart events he is still running the said business.

Further along with the answers given by the PW.1 if we perused Ex.P13 income tax returns in the assessment year of 2022-2023 the gross income of the petitioner was Rs.4,51,870/- and after the accident in the next assessment year ie., for the assessment year 2023-2024 the gross income of the petitioner was Rs.5,58,040/-.

Thereby along with the admissions of PW.1 in the cross-examination the Ex.P13 also reveals that after the accident also the income of the petitioner is increased and it is not reduced due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Thereby even though the PW.3 doctor assessed the physical disability it can be held that the said physical disability has not affected the functional disability which resulted in loss of income.
As answered by the PW.1 his income is not reduced.
No evidence or explanation is offered by the petitioner to hold that he has taken the assistance of other workers to run the business of Durga Mart and Events.
As such no evidence is available to consider that due to the physical disabilities caused to the petitioner he has sustained financial loss.
Accordingly, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'

That is to say as the Ravichandra vs Satyanarayanaraju K.V on 15 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167755220/
7 actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant,
he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'.

sentences.text: e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per Ex.P.8 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 6 days.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P7 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.

By considering the nature of the injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner has spent 6 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e.,
Rs.6,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
As per the evidence of PW.3 doctor the petitioner has sustained 30.77% of lower limb permanent disability wherein it effects the day to day life style of the petitioner.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
As per the evidence of PW.3 doctor at the time of recent clinical examination it shows that the fractures are united and implants are in situ.

The petitioner produced Ex.P14 letter issued by the Pramod hospital wherein they stated that the petitioner has to under go removal of NAIL and the cost of surgery for implant is approximately Rs.1,00,000/-.
The author of the Ex.P14 is not examined and the estimation is also not produced.
But as the implants are in situ there is need of another surgery for removal of implants.
As such Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 60,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 34,000/-
c) Towards loss of income  during laid down period Rs. 62,000/-

g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-

 _______________  Total Rs. 2,52,000/-
21.
Liability:- According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Car bearing No.KA-51-P-1954.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
The amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses is an amount awarded for future expenses.
Hence the amount awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carries any interest.
But the remaining amount shall carries the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of Rs.2,52,000/-
 (Rupees Two lakhs fifty two thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses), from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 08.03.2022.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained multiple injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Promed Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 08.03.2022 to 11.03.2022 and further admitted on 27.06.2022 to 28.06.2022, undergone operations and discharged with advice to take bed rest.
He has paid the Income Tax for the income of Rs.5,06,470/- for the assessment year of 2021-22.
As such he is not capable of discharging his duties and thus suffered loss of income.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. The respondent No.2- insurance company has filed written statement by denying the negligence and their liability.
But both the respondents have not lead any evidence to rebut the case of the petitioner.
In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.
16. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.
All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 08.03.2022 which is caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-P-1954. which belonging to respondent No.1.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary,
but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
